products.evidence: The displayed 472-residue product, independently matched to the official FASTA. Full-length human CWC27 and its C-terminal fragments bind CWC22 in PMID:32329775; this interaction is noncatalytic. Structural complex preparations do not resolve every detected molecule to this product.

The official 390-residue product is reconstructed by VSP_030082 (residues 385–391 replaced by DVTCTS) and VSP_030083 (392–472 absent). PMID:32329775 explicitly uses Q6UX04-2 and finds no retention by recombinant CWC22-S with or without EIF4A3. This is an assay-specific functional distinction, not evidence that the short product has no biological function.

ontology_scope.assessment: All-five-snRNP precatalytic definition does not fit the three-snRNP Bact structure.
General U2-type spliceosomal complex covers the major Bact experiment; typed parent of GO:0071005.
Post-first-cleavage minor state does not fit the trapped pre-branching Bact source.
General U12-type spliceosomal complex covers the actual minor Bact experiment; typed parent of GO:0071018.
Post-first-cleavage scope is supported contextually by the 2002 enriched C-complex target peptides; structural-stage tension remains.
Activated synonym does not remove the defined catalytically active state requirement.
U2 activated/step-1 term has a catalytic-state requirement; not substituted from Bact nomenclature alone.
U12 activated/step-1 term has a catalytic-state requirement; not substituted from Bact nomenclature alone.

Conserved-site folding mapping exceeds demonstrated CWC27-specific function and is marked over-annotated. Protein folding can be noncatalytic; the assay results do not refute every possible folding role.
Existing NOT kept at the actual standard-tetrapeptide assay scope.
Structural participation and human depletion support splicing involvement without intrinsic RNA catalysis.
Broad complex synthesis accommodates both major and minor spliceosomes and context-dependent stages.

core_molecular_function.label: splicing factor binding
core_molecular_function.evidence: PMID:32329775, main Figure 3 and Results on purified CWC27/CWC22 binding, short splice product, C-terminal fragments and interface structure.
core_molecular_function.scope: Reciprocal retention of purified bacterial recombinant CWC27 and CWC22-S (residues 100–665), with the CWC27 C-terminal region contacting CWC22 directly, supports this binding class. The tested 390-residue splice product did not support the interaction. EIF4A3 alone did not retain CWC27; no direct CWC27–EIF4A3 binding or RNA catalytic activity is inferred.
core_molecular_function.composition: One existing core retains GO:1990935. A product-scoped NEW IPI now represents direct CWC22 binding; all 16 original source objects remain exact, with only the folding review action changed.
